source_scope.paper: OpenSkill: Open-World Self-Evolution for LLM Agents

findings.claim: OpenSkill constructs skills and independent virtual verification anchors without target-task supervision, freezes the resulting skill before target evaluation, and reports ScienceWorld average reward 90.0 with Opus 4.6 and 85.3 with GPT 5.2.
findings.scope_guard: These ScienceWorld results establish the viability of proxy-verified open-world skill construction, not an isolated verifier-only ScienceWorld effect.

findings.claim: The virtual verifier is useful but not authoritative: on N=84 outcomes it reports 56.9% precision, 80.5% recall and 60.7% overall agreement with ground truth, while covering 120/135 (88.9%) sampled GT test intents. The paper also notes that open-world anchors can be noisy, outdated or contradictory and that virtual tasks can overestimate target quality.
findings.scope_guard: A proxy-verifier pass should not be promoted to final scientific acceptance; record anchor provenance and retain downstream/final evaluation separation.

findings.claim: At exact official GitHub revision 9de2f520..., the repository contains only project overview/assets and explicitly says core code is still forthcoming. The reported verifier/evolution mechanism is therefore not implementation-replayable from the current advertised repository revision.
findings.scope_guard: Absence claim is restricted to the exact official GitHub revision inspected; it does not exclude private or later artifacts.

protocol_implication.name: PROXY_VERIFIER_NONAUTHORITY_AND_ANCHOR_PROVENANCE
protocol_implication.rule: For proxy-built scientific verification, bind each test/verdict to independent source anchors and provenance, keep target-ground-truth leakage barriers explicit, and treat proxy pass as provisional evidence rather than final acceptance authority.
